text:
Christine Wong: heads up — breaker flapping bug is still present in staging after yesterday’s config tweak. Seeing rapid CLOSED→OPEN→HALF_OPEN→OPEN loops on the same (model, region, tier) within ~30–60s.

Here’s a snippet from routing-svc staging (us-east, model=rw-open-llama-70b, tier=standard):
```
2024-07-24T16:48:02.991Z INFO breaker_transition key=model=rw-open-llama-70b region=us-east tier=standard from=CLOSED to=OPEN reason=queue_depth_high q_depth=512 q_limit=512 cooldown_s=60
2024-07-24T16:48:33.114Z INFO breaker_transition key=model=rw-open-llama-70b region=us-east tier=standard from=OPEN to=HALF_OPEN reason=cooldown_elapsed elapsed_ms=30123 cooldown_ms=60000
2024-07-24T16:48:33.219Z INFO breaker_probe_result key=model=rw-open-llama-70b region=us-east tier=standard result=FAIL reason=gpu_sat_high gpu_util=0.98
2024-07-24T16:48:33.221Z INFO breaker_transition key=model=rw-open-llama-70b region=us-east tier=standard from=HALF_OPEN to=OPEN reason=probe_failed cooldown_s=60
2024-07-24T16:49:03.402Z INFO breaker_transition key=model=rw-open-llama-70b region=us-east tier=standard from=OPEN to=HALF_OPEN reason=cooldown_elapsed elapsed_ms=30181 cooldown_ms=60000
```
Note the elapsed_ms is ~30s but we’re treating it as if cooldown elapsed. Looks like the comparison is busted (ms vs s?) or we’re persisting the wrong timestamp.

Grafana panel shows transitions spiking to ~20/min for that key. This will definitely murder error mix + trigger retry storms if it makes it past flags.

I opened a hotfix PR with a minimal change + regression test: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18519

Rafael Mendes: ty. That log is pretty damning — we’re half-opening at ~30s consistently which screams unit mismatch or int truncation.

Do we see it across keys or just the hottest one? Also, is this only after config reload, or steady-state?

Christine Wong: across multiple keys but worst on the hottest (standard tier). Also happens steady-state; not tied to reload.

Repro steps I used:
1) perf-canary staging “step spike” to 3x baseline for 2 min
2) let it drain
3) watch breaker transitions + shed rate

Even after load returns to normal, the breaker does this oscillation for ~10 min.

Tomáš Novák: if the half-open probe is failing due to gpu_util still high, it’s expected to go OPEN again — but not expected to go HALF_OPEN at 30s when cooldown=60s.

In addition to the unit fix, can we make sure we’re not doing “cooldown elapsed” based on wall clock skew between nodes? If state is stored centrally and each replica uses local time, that can also get weird.

Peter Holtz: +1. I took a quick look at staging traces — the state store write shows `opened_at_ms` but reader side is comparing to `cooldown_s * 1000` sometimes and sometimes not (depending on code path). Might be why it’s consistently ~30s (one path halving the value?)

Christine Wong: yeah that’s what PR is addressing. We had two helpers:
- `cooldownElapsed(openedAtMs, cooldownMs)`
- `cooldownElapsed(openedAtMs, cooldownS)` (older)

One call site in the HALF_OPEN scheduler was still passing seconds to the ms helper. So effectively cooldown became 60ms *or* 60/2? depending on conversion. In practice we’re hitting ~30s due to `cooldown/2` path for probe window.

PR makes the interface explicit: cooldown always stored + passed as ms, removes the seconds helper, and adds a test that fails if HALF_OPEN happens before cooldown.

Mina Haddad: thanks for catching. If we’re merging this, can we get it into today’s staging build? Routing team is trying to validate breaker behavior before we sign off Phase 1.

Benji Okafor: from rollout side: we can keep breaker feature flag OFF in staging for the routing path until this is in, but we still want to run perf-canary with it ON soon. What’s the ETA on review?

Allison Grant: observability note: if this flaps like this in prod, it’s going to explode cardinality in transition counters (plus pages if someone accidentally keys alerts on transitions). +1 to fixing before we tune any alerting.

Ethan Park: also worth confirming control-plane responsiveness — if the breaker store gets hammered by transitions, we’ll see knock-on effects.

Rafael Mendes: I’ll review PR now. Christine can you also add a quick note in PR description about the impact (flapping -> increased 429/503 churn + retry amplification) so release has context?

Christine Wong: yep, added. Also added a staging log query for verification:
`index=routing-svc env=staging "breaker_transition" | stats count by key, from, to`

Tomáš Novák: once merged, can we rerun the same step spike and confirm:
- transitions/min drops
- breaker stays OPEN for full cooldown
- half-open probe count is bounded (no probe storms)

Christine Wong: plan:
- merge hotfix
- deploy routing-svc staging
- rerun perf-canary scenario
- share before/after screenshots in this thread + link to perf run

Benji Okafor: if it looks good, I’ll also update the rollout checklist doc to include “transition rate sanity check” as a go/no-go metric.

Rafael Mendes: approved from SRE side. Waiting on one more routing LGTM then let’s ship to staging.

Mina Haddad: LGTM on the routing side. Merge it.

Christine Wong: merged. Staging deploy queued.

[deploy-bot] routing-svc staging deploy started (build #8821, commit 7f2c1a9)

[deploy-bot] routing-svc staging deploy finished successfully

Christine Wong: reran the step spike. After hotfix:
- transitions down from ~20/min to ~1/min for the hot key
- OPEN held for full ~60s (first HALF_OPEN at 60–62s)
- no rapid OPEN↔HALF_OPEN oscillation

Posting the “before/after” panel links (staging):
- breaker transitions: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/breaker-transitions-staging?from=1721778000&to=1721790000
- shed rate + q depth: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/overload-shed-staging?from=1721778000&to=1721790000

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: thanks. Let’s keep an eye on it for the rest of the day, but this looks like the root cause.

Allison Grant: awesome. once this is in prod, we should baseline “expected transition rate” per key to prevent regressions.

Tomáš Novák: +1. Also, can we add this as a “known failure mode” in the runbook draft: high transition rate = likely flapping (check cooldown + timestamps).

Christine Wong: will do; I’ll add a small section to the runbook PR and link back here.
